rv.q: It makes The Father more compelling than ever.
What Zeller catches admirably is the way Andre, a retired engineer, still clings to an authority he is no longer capable of executing.
The Father ‘s a play you have to see to know yourself, and those you love, better.
This is a truly marvellous turn from Cranham, easily one of the great performances of the year and the decade.
It’s an uncomfortable performance, brilliant in its understanding and its detail.
The central contrivance is intellectually engaging yet at ninety minutes it leaves you plenty of time for dinner before the train back to the suburbs and contains nothing to put you off your food.

cn.t: Critics largely rave about Zeller's Alzheimer's drama, praising Cranham's performance and its disorienting first-person perspective. One dissenting voice finds it over-engineered, but most call it a profound theatrical experience.
